races.name: Enjoy A Bostin Day At The Races With SFRacing Club Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hauteluce
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Roger-bred type with only one start (5th over 8f on standard going), Ed Walker yard in solid 14-day form; unknown style makes mapping impossible but the unexposed angle and similar going experience gives her an each-way profile if the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Fair on debut at Lingfield, beaten nine lengths in a maiden though she showed clear inexperience throughout; off the track for over six months since, which is a concern, but a sire-miler dam-stayer cross suggests the trip could suit better beyond a mile as she fills her frame. Lightly raced with scope.

runners_data.name: Ice Show
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's filly arrives 23 days fresh with three placed runs in soft-to-good ground; her genuine style is hold-up but the field's depth of rear-runners means she is likely to find herself racing more prominently than ideal, discounting her chance in a truly run race.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 9¼ lengths at Thirsk last time when the shorter trip looked against her — the hood is on for the first time today and a top course jockey takes the saddle; her dam was successful at 7f but this distance could still be a stretch. May fare better in handicap company over further.

runners_data.name: Salamis Bay
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway's 62-rated filly has hit the frame on standard going twice from four runs and steps up to 9½f; her hold-up style is natural and she has some staying breadth, though her flat finishing record means she needs a stronger gallop than Peace Belle is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Ground concerns ease today — she appeared to find soft conditions against her at Yarmouth last time and this AW surface suits, having stayed ten furlongs reliably; the current assignment looks less demanding than recent ones and she holds clear claims. Tricky to assess accurately, but on merit one of the main dangers.

runners_data.name: Sweet Horizon
runners_data.note: Tom Clover debutante with no form or going data available, entirely unknown style; Jack Mitchell takes the ride for a trainer 3-from-16 over 14 days, so treat as a pure wildcard who could be anything.
runners_data.comment: A Lope Y Fernandez filly who is a half-sister to 1m2f performer Marama; bred to find her range around a mile-plus and attracted a solid yearling price. Worth a look at market interest before the off — the pedigree is more encouraging than debut unknowns might suggest.

runners_data.name: Crack Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a single run that ended 12th over 16f on good ground with a noted fade — a likely stayer who may not see out this 9½f at a pace quick enough to test her, and the lightly-raced flag adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Showed little in an Amateurs' bumper at Worcester on her only previous start — well beaten and unable to make any impact — and has plenty to demonstrate making the switch to the Flat. Hard to fancy at this stage.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner with a Wolverhampton-like profile — won over 16f on good going — and Jennie Candlish sends her 80 days fresh; her style_fit flag reflects the shorter trip relative to her winning form, but on pace terms she controls this race and has first run on everyone.
runners_data.comment: A mare who landed a bumper earlier but struggled in a Grade 2 mares' NH Flat race last time out, though that was a stiff assignment; effective at two miles on good ground and usually held up, she can translate bumper form to the Flat. Off a short break but one of the main threats.

runners_data.name: Cherringham
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's once-raced filly finished fifth over 10f on soft, now stretching to 9½f on standard polytrack for Ray Dawson; the step to this surface and trip is unknown quantity but Varian's class and the extra yardage could unlock improvement.
runners_data.comment: Ran freely on debut at Lingfield but showed enough ability through the race before fading to a 5¼-length fifth; the faster surface here looks a significant upgrade on conditions and she is bred to improve. Trainer in strong current form — she looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Blue Celestial
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly has the most exposed form in the field — four placed efforts on standard going — and her 5-from-8 placed record on similar surfaces makes her the most reliable form reference; Hector Crouch knows her well and she should travel in a good position from a 28-day break.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Nottingham last time, beaten four and a half lengths in a handicap where she lacked the necessary pace, but she handles today's surface and has a recent placed effort on the AW to her name; a trainer in excellent current form adds appeal. Stamina at this trip is the question.

runners_data.name: Midnight Media
runners_data.note: William Muir & Chris Grassick's 55-rated filly has a poor form string (including finishing 9th, 12th on standard going) and carries a fades-in-finish note; though her natural preference is to race from the rear, the crowded hold-up contingent means she is mapped in midfield — a position that is unlikely to improve her chance meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of the places at Windsor last time where stamina again appeared the issue — a recurring concern given her record — and she has been thoroughly inconsistent in recent outings; effective at a mile on the AW, she needs things to fall her way. Hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Miss Mambo
runners_data.note: Gay Kelleway runs her alongside stablemate Salamis Bay; a hold-up type by inclination but bumped into midfield by the field's structural overcrowding, she has placed on soft going and carries blinkers — any headgear effect needs monitoring, though her OR of 53 is the lowest in the field.
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers are applied after she appeared to find this trip a stretch here last time, beaten over eight lengths; effective at six to eight furlongs on the surface and the headgear change adds a spark, though stamina questions remain. Form has been patchy but worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Sunshine And Roses
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's filly has three placed efforts on standard going from ten runs and is tactically versatile, though her true preference for racing from the rear is compromised here by the sheer number of similar types; the style_fit discount applies, and her best chance arrives if the pace collapses rather than if she can dictate.
runners_data.comment: A flat Windsor run last time wants forgetting, but she handles AW conditions well over seven to nine furlongs and this looks less demanding than recent assignments; the trainer's poor current spell is the main concern. She has the ability to get involved if back near her best.

races.paceDynamic: Peace Belle is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, she should control tempo from the gates and set a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m1½f Wolverhampton flat. With the redistribution pressure noted, Ice Show, Sunshine And Roses, Midnight Media and Miss Mambo are all natural hold-up types who are effectively pushed into midfield slots on the map because the field holds more genuine off-the-pace operators than the rear positions can accommodate — Peace Belle is most likely to actually secure the rail and dictate. A controlled lead on standard Wolverhampton polytrack over nearly a mile and two typically rewards horses who can race prominently, travel into the race from a handy position, and produce a clean turn of foot from two furlongs out rather than those relying on a late charge into a modest gallop. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent and mid-division horses with scope to improve and clean finishing gears hold the structural advantage, while true hold-up types face the double penalty of a slow pace and being shuffled further back than they would choose.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Peace Belle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Peace Belle goes unchallenged to the front and controls a steady, uncontested gallop from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: If Peace Belle goes unchallenged to the front and controls a steady, uncontested gallop from flag to finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Picks Her Off
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling prominently in second or third tracks Peace Belle into the straight and produces a stronger finish.
scenarios.body: If a horse travelling prominently in second or third tracks Peace Belle into the straight and produces a stronger finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Filly Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses enough in the straight to allow a mid-division horse to pick through tired rivals.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses enough in the straight to allow a mid-division horse to pick through tired rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If positional jostling disrupts the field mid-race and an unconsidered runner finds a clear run at the death.
scenarios.body: If positional jostling disrupts the field mid-race and an unconsidered runner finds a clear run at the death.

watchPoints.text: Peace Belle leads unopposed — if she builds even a two-length buffer turning for home unchallenged, her rivals racing from midfield or further back will have almost no mechanism to close the gap on a standard Wolverhampton surface.

Ice Show, Midnight Media, Miss Mambo and Sunshine And Roses are all natural hold-up types squeezed into midfield — watch for potential crowding and interference on the back straight if several jockeys attempt to find the same rail gap simultaneously.

Sweet Horizon is an unknown quantity on debut for Tom Clover — if she breaks smartly and challenges Peace Belle for the early lead, the pace dynamic changes entirely and the whole shape of the race is re-set.

Blue Celestial's placed record on standard going (4 from 8 on-surface runs) is the clearest form anchor in this field — watch her position at the turn; if she is travelling smoothly in the first three, she becomes the most likely beneficiary of Scenario B.

Crack Of Thunder's only run ended in a heavy fade over 16f on good ground — monitor her in the early stages; if she drops away before the straight, it confirms this trip is likely too sharp and she can be safely dismissed in future.

races.name: First Windsorlot Then Voltaic & Now Teardrops Handicap

runners_data.name: Taradif
runners_data.note: A 129-day absence is a real flag here, and while the fading-in-finish flag compounds the concern, its natural habitat is deep hold-up racing — squeezed into a midfield slot in this shape, the horse is denied its preferred late-running position and sim-going figures show zero wins or places from two comparable starts.|
runners_data.comment: Making a well-beaten handicap debut in France last time, Taradif comes here with a 129-day gap since last running and must prove his form translates to British conditions; first-time tongue-tie is fitted but he sits at the foot of our rankings and the mark looks stiff.

runners_data.name: Aerial Silk
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's yard is in form at 4/15 over the past fortnight, and Billy Loughnane takes the ride, but the horse's instinct is to race from the rear — slotted into midfield by circumstance rather than design, it must overcome an unnatural position on a track that often exposes those who lose their rhythm in the first half of the race.|
runners_data.comment: Showed reasonable form before a flat effort at Haydock last time when stepped up to 1m; Aerial Silk must prove his stamina over this longer trip but has a top course jockey in the saddle and returns after a short break on a surface he handles.

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford have been busy (4/27 T14) and Jack Mitchell is a booking worth noting, but Faeberon's AW history (the one AW sim-going run produced a placing) is thin — the horse wants to come from the back of the field in its own time, and being forced into midfield on a pace-controlled day will blunt that style significantly.|
runners_data.comment: Putting in a solid handicap debut at Thirsk last time, going down by 2 lengths off a mark 1lb below today’s, Faeberon showed he can compete at this level; first-time cheekpieces are tried and he stays well, though he has more to prove here.

runners_data.name: Magician Of Riga
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's improver has won back-to-back at this exact trip on Standard AW going and boasts the strongest sim-going record in the field (2W3P from 7 runs); a true hold-up type who gets to operate from his natural rear position, he is the one genuine late threat if the pace quickens sufficiently.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by a neck at Southwell last time off a mark 3lb below today’s, Magician Of Riga has two wins in recent starts and remains well treated overall; a longer trip than today’s would suit better but he handles the all-weather and comes off a short break.

runners_data.name: Eljowhary
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's colt is fresh off a 20-day turnaround and has the 'hg:h' headgear flag, but three runs all show finishes of 4-6-6 so progression has been minimal; races from hold-up in the style that suits it, though sim-going form (0W0P from two Standard runs) does not inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Appeared to idle when only fourth at Windsor last time, Eljowhary is expected to benefit from stepping up in trip and moving into handicap company; he handles the all-weather and a first-time hood is fitted to sharpen him up.

runners_data.name: Windbreaker
runners_data.note: William Haggas is firing at 11/57 over 14 days and Cieren Fallon is a top-level booking; has placed at this trip twice on varying ground and brings a consistent hold-up profile — of the rear-tracking horses, its recent course-relevant form (3rd on Standard) makes it one of the more credible late movers.|
runners_data.comment: Denied a clear run at a crucial stage last time and beaten 3½ lengths off a mark 1lb above today’s, Windbreaker rates better than bare results suggest; well supported in recent outings with more to come, he tops our figures here.

runners_data.name: Court Of Stars
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old is the most naturally placed horse in this race, sitting in the prominent role it has occupied when winning and placing on AW Standard surfaces (1W3P from 8 sim-going runs); PLJ has a clean tactical record and this horse's profile — speed-to-stay, prominent, handles Polytrack — is tailor-made for a pace-controlled contest.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a race at Kempton off a lower mark earlier in the season, Court Of Stars ran to form last time despite missing the start, finishing fourth beaten only 2 lengths off this mark; consistent throughout and from an inside draw, she is a solid danger.

runners_data.name: The Stone Power
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett sends this one out as the lone confirmed front-runner, and with 8/51 T14 Beckett is in decent form; Hector Crouch takes over, but the style-fit flag is relevant — The Stone Power may set the terms but its own winning chance is tempered by a record that includes no wins from four Standard AW runs and a tendency to be caught late.|
runners_data.comment: Struggling to match the pace on his handicap debut at Newbury last time, The Stone Power was beaten 5¼ lengths and may simply have needed the run; he rates second on our figures and the extra distance on the all-weather should suit better.

runners_data.name: Silky Lass
runners_data.note: K R Burke is among the most prolific AW trainers in the data (6/51 T14) and Silky Lass has an outstanding sim-going record of 1W6P from nine Standard AW runs — its natural instinct is to race from the rear but finds itself mapped into midfield; the consistent placed form means it can still be competitive if it settles and finds a clear run.|
runners_data.comment: Outpaced after being held up last time here but still placed second beaten 7 lengths behind a well-treated rival, Silky Lass ran well in the circumstances; effective over 1m-9f on the all-weather and in good form, she can go close again.

runners_data.name: Just A Gambler
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner (10/72 T14) has multiple wins and places but its one sim-going AW start produced a mid-pack finish, and being a natural hold-up horse pushed into midfield reduces its ability to produce the late surge it relies on; Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a small compensation but the overall package is modest at OR 64.|
runners_data.comment: Had his chance at Hamilton last time but went down by 7 lengths in fourth, dipping below his prior level; Just A Gambler handles the all-weather at 8f but recent efforts have been unimpressive and he needs to find more.

races.paceDynamic: The Stone Power is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals likely to press him hard from the jump, he should carve out a controlled, unhurried pace on the Wolverhampton Polytrack over this mile-and-a-half furlongs. That measured gallop is likely to compress the race into a tactical exercise through the middle portion, setting up a decisive finish around the home turn rather than a true stamina test. Court Of Stars, travelling prominently, is best placed to capitalise on the first run at the leader, while the hold-up brigade must cover ground from well back on a track that rewards those who travel close to the pace. This shape firmly favours prominent-racing types who can time their challenge without needing a strong early pace to string the field out — genuine closers will find the steady tempo gives them too much to do. The field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear: Taradif, Aerial Silk, Faeberon, Silky Lass, and Just A Gambler are all natural hold-up horses pushed into midfield slots, with Magician Of Riga, Windbreaker, and Eljowhary the most likely to actually secure rearward positions given their consistent hold-up profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stone Power Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If The Stone Power leads without serious early pressure and controls a sedate tempo into the straight.
scenarios.body: If The Stone Power leads without serious early pressure and controls a sedate tempo into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close-Tracking Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out modestly but those who tracked second or third through the race find momentum in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out modestly but those who tracked second or third through the race find momentum in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong enough to exhaust the front two and create a genuine gap for horses finishing from off the pace.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves strong enough to exhaust the front two and create a genuine gap for horses finishing from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse Into Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed midfield runners interfere with each other's runs or overcrowd the pocket between the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If several of the redistributed midfield runners interfere with each other's runs or overcrowd the pocket between the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Court Of Stars is the standout tactical beneficiary — if Pierre-Louis Jamin slots it directly behind The Stone Power in the first three furlongs, watch for an unchallenged challenge from the quarter-mile pole that the rest of the field is powerless to match.

With Taradif, Aerial Silk, Faeberon, Silky Lass, and Just A Gambler all occupying the same manufactured midfield band, severe crowding around Wolverhampton's home turn is a live risk — any horse drawn wide in that pocket should be monitored closely from the half-mile mark.

Magician Of Riga's back-to-back wins at this trip on this surface make him dangerous if The Stone Power's sedate early pace somehow quickens mid-race — Joe Leavy must avoid getting buried in the midfield traffic to land the late blow this horse is capable of.

The Stone Power's unbeaten-in-pace role belies a win-free AW record; watch whether Hector Crouch elects to increase the tempo entering the back straight to try to stretch the field — if he does, the race shape shifts entirely towards Magician Of Riga and away from the tracking types.

Windbreaker's 10-day turnaround for William Haggas (11/57 T14) suggests the yard is content with the horse's condition; if Cieren Fallon can find a prominent position despite the horse's natural hold-up style, it becomes a more dangerous runner than its odds may reflect.

races.name: Oldboys Fieldsman The Legend And Undercurfew Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sonbelievable
runners_data.comment: Showed signs of inexperience at Windsor on his only start but did finish with purpose once things clicked, though still well beaten; speed in the pedigree is encouraging and there is scope to do better with that debut run under the belt.

runners_data.name: Gallant Pioneer
runners_data.comment: Debut runner by top-class middle-distance sire Ulysses, a half-brother to 6f performer Boma Green, so the trip question hinges on which influence prevails; the stable is in excellent current form, which is the main thing in his favour here.

runners_data.name: Miss Nightcap
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in maidens with her Newbury second last time — beaten a length — representing solid form that has been backed up by subsequent results; a wind operation before her debut has clearly not hampered her. Effective at six furlongs on fast ground, she holds the best claims in this field.

runners_data.name: Captive Beauty
runners_data.comment: Two runs in Ireland produced little — beaten eight lengths in a claimer at Gowran Park last time — and much remains to be demonstrated on this switch to Flat conditions after a short break; the trainer is in good form and the speed-stamina pedigree mix is workable, though this asks considerable questions.

runners_data.name: Harry Rocket
runners_data.comment: Back after nearly a year off the track, Harry Rocket was well beaten on his only start at Leicester, and much remains to be demonstrated from that forgettable debut; a sprint-miler cross pedigree offers little comfort at this distance. Hard to fancy on these figures.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Jive
runners_data.comment: His Salisbury run 19 days ago — beaten 8¼ lengths in a novice — hinted at development as a debut outing, though plenty more is needed; sire brings speed and dam offers some stamina, a mix that may suit today's trip.

runners_data.name: Hozam
runners_data.comment: Promising on debut here when third, beaten two lengths in a maiden — ran freely and struck the front ahead of his time, but the AW form is solid and there is clear scope for improvement. A top course jockey takes the ride and the mile trip on this surface suits.

runners_data.name: Rogue Federation
runners_data.comment: Debut at Yarmouth yielded a fifth, beaten over eight lengths in a novice, leaving plenty to find here; the 6-7f pedigree suggests today's trip may be on the sharp side. Hard to get excited about on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Rubistar
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred filly who looked inexperienced and appeared to find six furlongs beyond her at Leicester last time, beaten over eight lengths in a maiden; there is a suggestion the trip may now suit at three, though plenty remains to prove given the modest figures.

runners_data.name: Chasse Patate
runners_data.comment: Second at Lingfield last time, beaten just over two lengths in a novice, represents solid AW form and her debut efforts have been backed up since; there is a case for further improvement here and she is effective at seven furlongs on the surface. One of the main threats.

runners_data.name: Elsa Tan
runners_data.comment: A Cable Bay filly who is a full-sister to smart 6f performer Silver Samurai, and another sibling has gone in over six furlongs second time out — the sprint pedigree is compelling; she is likely to benefit from having this run first but the family form gives genuine reason for optimism.

runners_data.name: Vichenza
runners_data.comment: Consistent third at Leicester last time, beaten four and a half lengths in a novice, where she raced freely early and flattened out late, but still ran to her mark; sprint-bred and handles six furlongs well on a sound surface, with further progress on the cards. A legitimate danger.

races.name: Francesi Wins Again For SF Racing Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Four Fifty
runners_data.note: Top-speed figures are minimal on Standard going (1 win/place from 11 similar-going runs) and the horse's natural style is deep hold-up, though the crowded hold-up division means securing even a midfield berth may be optimistic; the 23-day break and form string including a 0 raises concern.|
runners_data.comment: In poor shape at Bath last time, beaten six lengths in a handicap, and his reliable form is firmly over shorter trips of seven to eight furlongs; a first-time tongue-tie is fitted but stamina over sixteen furlongs looks a serious concern. Hard to justify on current evidence.

runners_data.name: Individualiste
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead as the sole pace-setter despite being a genuine prominent type — the eight-year-old has raced over marathon trips before but has zero wins or places from 15 similar-going runs at Standard; the 18-day return and apprentice booking (Millie Wonnacott, 5lb) are relevant context for how the pace is managed.|
runners_data.comment: After missing the break at Kempton last time he over-raced in an attempt to recover, ultimately finishing well beaten in a handicap; form looks to be heading the wrong way and he needs to show considerably more than recent outings have offered.

runners_data.name: Edwardtheninth
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Standard going (1W from 10 similar-going runs) and recent form shows a rallying 1 last time, though Ruth Jefferson has had a quiet recent 14-day spell (0/3); a natural hold-up horse that will need to find space in a congested rear group.|
runners_data.comment: Landing a handicap at Newcastle last time by three-quarters of a length off a mark 2lb lower, he appears back to something like his best; effective at 14-16 furlongs on the AW and still on a workable mark, he could build further on that run now a win is back under the belt.

runners_data.name: The Craftymaster
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's string is red-hot at 10/39 over 14 days and this six-year-old has two wins and three places from 15 similar-going runs — the strongest trainer angle in the race; races from the rear by style and has the course-distance profile to challenge late over the marathon trip.|
runners_data.comment: Hampered at a critical point at Bath last time, which excuses a 3½-length defeat off a mark 7lb lower than today; a genuine AW stayer who thrives at 14-16 furlongs, with a first-time tongue-tie fitted and a top course trainer in his corner. A forgivable run and capable of going close.

runners_data.name: The Bay Warrior
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride and the horse has an excellent Standard-going record (2W5P from 14 runs), though the step up to 2m½f from recent 12f runs is a stamina query worth noting; genuine hold-up type with proven course form.|
runners_data.comment: Back in form at Leicester last time, going down by only three-quarters of a length off a mark 1lb below today's, and returning to the AW where almost all his best efforts have come; first-time cheekpieces applied though stamina over sixteen furlongs is unproven. A genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Qaaeadd
runners_data.note: Has failed to win or place in 11 similar-going runs and the recent form (75795) is uninspiring; a natural hold-up horse that is likely to find this trip and the crowded hold-up division working against it, with Jack Callan's 3lb claim the main positive.|
runners_data.comment: Kept to his modest level at Lingfield last time, beaten over six lengths in a classified race, with the form suggesting others here hold stronger claims; effective over seven to ten furlongs but today's sixteen furlongs looks a significant stamina test. A first-time tongue-tie changes little on these figures.

runners_data.name: Man Of Riddles
runners_data.note: 131-day absence (49 days since jockey's last ride) is a significant fitness concern for an eight-year-old with no wins from 15 similar-going runs; natural hold-up style suits the race shape in theory but the layoff and modest form (4078-0) make relying on this horse risky.|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers are fitted as he returns from an unsuccessful hurdles foray at Ludlow, where he appeared to find the trip a struggle; suited by two miles on the AW and the switch back to this surface should help, though current form gives cause for caution regardless of the headgear.

runners_data.name: Ebendi
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old has finished 7th seven times in recent outings and has only 2 similar-going runs from 15 on Standard surfaces (0W0P); the consistent tendency to finish mid-pack without threatening suggests the race shape would need to be perfect for this horse to factor.|
runners_data.comment: Winless and thoroughly out of form — a run of seventh-place finishes culminating in a six-length defeat at Newcastle — with nothing of note on the Flat since 2022; a hurdles spell added little either. Hard to find merit in his cause on present evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Individualiste is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 2m½f Wolverhampton handicap, redistributed to the lead because no natural front-runner is present — their prominent style makes them the most likely to dictate from the front over this marathon trip. With eight hold-up types in the field and only Individualiste providing any early structure, the gallop should be steady to moderate, creating a genuinely unhurried early tempo that will compress the field through the long back straight. That controlled pace scenario strongly favours the hold-up runners who can travel well mid-race and quicken late, particularly those with proven stamina at this trip and sound form on Standard Wolverhampton surfaces. Several horses tagged REDISTRIBUTED — including Four Fifty, Edwardtheninth, Qaaeadd, Man Of Riddles and Ebendi — are natural hold-up types shown in midfield purely because the map cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; The Craftymaster and The Bay Warrior, with their genuine hold-up profiles and course-relevant form, are best placed to secure their favoured positions and benefit from a late-run shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Individualiste sets a modest, uncontested tempo that keeps the field bunched and sets up a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Individualiste sets a modest, uncontested tempo that keeps the field bunched and sets up a sprint finish from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Individualiste Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Individualiste's uncontested lead allows them to steal enough first-run advantage that the field cannot reel them in over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Individualiste's uncontested lead allows them to steal enough first-run advantage that the field cannot reel them in over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Stayer Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If any horse in the chasing pack travels powerfully enough to make a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than waiting for a late sprint.
scenarios.body: If any horse in the chasing pack travels powerfully enough to make a sustained run from two furlongs out rather than waiting for a late sprint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Organise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the field fails to produce a meaningful finish, leaving the result to whoever positions best from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely and the field fails to produce a meaningful finish, leaving the result to whoever positions best from the home turn.

watchPoints.text: Watch The Craftymaster — Tony Carroll's 10/39 14-day strike rate combined with two wins and three places on similar going makes this horse the standout trainer/form combination in the race.

Watch Individualiste's early gallop closely — if the pace is excessively slow, the entire field will be hunting for position simultaneously from the home turn, creating significant crowding among the hold-up types.
Watch The Bay Warrior's stamina under Silvestre De Sousa — the step from 12f to 2m½f is a significant jump and if the horse fades late it could impede closers coming through on the inside rail.

Watch Man Of Riddles' market moves given the 131-day layoff — any market support despite the absence would suggest connections are confident in fitness, which would change the dynamics of the hold-up group significantly.

Watch Edwardtheninth for an early position battle — Kyle McHugh (7lb) on a genuine hold-up type in a field full of hold-up types means securing any position at the rear cleanly will be a task in itself.

races.name: Alfred Cove You Will Always Be A Star Handicap

runners_data.name: Em Jay Kay
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with genuine Standard-going form (2 wins, 7 places from 14 similar-going runs), but 107 days off the track is a significant fitness query for trainer Phil McEntee, who is 0/2 in the last 14 days; headgear (hood/p) worn previously.
runners_data.comment: Had every chance in this grade last time but was still beaten 8 lengths here; first-time cheekpieces and sitting just 1lb above his last winning mark are small pluses, though Em Jay Kay returns from a 107-day break and draws wide.

runners_data.name: King David
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type whose recent form has been over Good ground — the switch back to Standard at Wolverhampton (4th, 6th in last two visits) suggests he handles it adequately but has not sparkled; trainer Gay Kelleway 0/4 in last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: AW form looks the key for King David, who was driven too hard in a turf handicap at Bath last time and beaten over 8 lengths; first-time tongue-tie and blinkers are fitted here, but a wide draw and a long winless run limit the appeal.

runners_data.name: Teardrops
runners_data.note: Improved horse whose last five runs on Standard going show a consistent placing record (3 wins, 8 places from 14 similar runs), and a 7lb claim for Myla Coppins could be a live booking; 27 days since last run is a straightforward prep.
runners_data.comment: Off the back of a flat display in a higher-grade event here, Teardrops must come back to form at a more suitable level; the trainer knows this track well, though the wide draw and a winless recent run limit confidence.

runners_data.name: White Umbrella
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will get a soft lead from the gates; a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 is attached because the horse is technically racing out of its deepest comfort zone, though in this context its lead role is entirely natural given the absence of challengers.
runners_data.comment: Back on the all-weather having struggled on turf at Catterick last time, White Umbrella arrives in first-time cheekpieces after 48 days off; she handles the surface and has placed in similar company before, but form has been inconsistent lately.

runners_data.name: Master Dandy
runners_data.note: A horse whose true instinct is to race at the rear — placed in the midfield on the map only because the field is overloaded with hold-up types; best run in this sequence was a win over 5f Standard and has been tried in blinkers/tongue tie, suggesting the trainer is actively managing him.
runners_data.comment: Master Dandy has won twice in recent starts with his best form on the all-weather at shorter trips; he went well below that level on turf at Thirsk last time, but runs off his last winning mark in first-time tongue-tie and blinkers.

runners_data.name: Thanks Dad
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield slot on the map given the cluster of closers in this race; recent form on Standard going is thin (7/15 similar runs placing) and the last two Wolverhampton runs were both double-figure finishes, making confidence hard to justify.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6 lengths at Brighton last time, Thanks Dad arrives without a win in recent outings and with a cold trainer record; first-time tongue-tie and visor are fitted but he is ranked last on our figures and needs a significant step forward.

runners_data.name: Alafdhal
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran that naturally wants to come from behind — shown in midfield here only because of redistribution pressure; visored, and has solid Standard-going credentials (14/15 runs in similar conditions), though recent form figures (9,12,7,5,9) do not scream imminent winner.
runners_data.comment: Pulled too hard at Yarmouth last time and beaten 9½ lengths, Alafdhal needs to settle better; back on the surface he handles best and below his last competitive mark, with a top course jockey in first-time visor, though the widest draw is a concern.

runners_data.name: Trust Sergei
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type whose last five runs are entirely on Standard or AW-Standard going (9/14 placing record); his most recent outing was a 2nd over 5f and stepping back up to 6f at Wolverhampton could suit, though the 54-day gap between runs is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Back to form over a shorter trip here last time, Trust Sergei went down by just 1¼ lengths off the same mark; he can be inconsistent and comes off a short break, but his record at this course makes him a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (0 wins but regularly finishes 2nd-5th) whose hold-up style has been forced into a midfield mapping; best efforts have come over 7f on Standard, and dropping to 6f here may not be ideal — trainer Scott Dixon 1/20 in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Running to form at Chepstow last time where he went down by only 1½ lengths off this mark, On Key has been consistently involved; yet to score, but he handles this surface well and the inside draw is no drawback.

runners_data.name: Last Outlaw
runners_data.note: The longest absence in the field at 137 days off the track for a horse whose best form figures over 6f Standard show no win and no place in the last five runs; the redistribution to midfield reflects the field dynamic rather than any change in natural racing style.
runners_data.comment: Returning from 137 days off, Last Outlaw made little impact at Southwell last time and performances have slipped back in recent starts; the mark is now considerably lower, however, and he handles this surface and trip, which gives him a slim chance.

runners_data.name: Sunlit Sea
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Sir Mark Prescott with a strong recent strike rate (2/16 in last 14 days); has placed four times from seven runs on similar going and a headgear flag suggests switching gear — 13 days since last run keeps fitness sharp, and the lighter weight (131lbs) is an asset.
runners_data.comment: Consistent on the all-weather before her latest run, Sunlit Sea was beaten 8½ lengths at Carlisle in headgear that clearly did not suit; first-time cheekpieces are tried here, she draws from stall 1, and she tops our figures in this field.

runners_data.name: Barry The Worm
runners_data.note: A horse that has won at Wolverhampton over 6f Standard and genuinely wants to race prominently — placed in midfield on the map because the field is congested at the front end, not because he lacks early pace; 19 days since last run and trainer Edward Smyth-Osbourne 0/5 in last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: A winner on this surface, Barry The Worm was too free at Salisbury last time and faded down the field; first-time cheekpieces are fitted here and he handles the all-weather well — if able to settle, the ability is there.

runners_data.name: Porfin
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old with solid Standard-going numbers (12/15 similar runs, 1 win 5 places) who is naturally a hold-up type pushed into a midfield display position by redistribution; the step down to OR 48 gives him a weight advantage but trainer Phil McEntee's recent 14-day form is quiet.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough at a modest level, Porfin was never able to get into contention at Bath last time and finished fourth beaten 4 lengths; first-time cheekpieces are added and he handles any surface over this trip, though he remains winless in recent outings.

races.paceDynamic: White Umbrella is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 13-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into an uncontested, controlled gallop from the front on this Standard Wolverhampton 6f. The absence of early pressure means the pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching, creating a rhythm that suits a relaxed leader over a trip where Wolverhampton's straight finish rewards those who travel kindly. With so many horses in this field naturally inclined to race prominently — Barry The Worm, Master Dandy, Thanks Dad and others are genuine front-end or prominent types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map purely because the field is saturated with them — a contested early position battle is still possible, but White Umbrella holds the clearest draw on the front end. The race shape ultimately favours horses with tactical versatility that can sit just off the controlled pace and pick up through the final two furlongs, making prominent-to-midfield closers the most advantaged profile, particularly those with strong Standard-going form at this course.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: White Umbrella Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If White Umbrella gets a clean break and no prominent rival seriously contests the lead, allowing a sustainable, unforced gallop.
scenarios.body: If White Umbrella gets a clean break and no prominent rival seriously contests the lead, allowing a sustainable, unforced gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rivals Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Barry The Worm or Master Dandy force their way closer to the pace early and the tempo quickens, setting up a two-furlong dash.
scenarios.body: If Barry The Worm or Master Dandy force their way closer to the pace early and the tempo quickens, setting up a two-furlong dash.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field fans wide in the straight, creating a proper end-to-end test.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field fans wide in the straight, creating a proper end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Turns Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If White Umbrella sets a very slow early pace and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint from halfway.
scenarios.body: If White Umbrella sets a very slow early pace and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint from halfway.

watchPoints.text: White Umbrella's gate break is critical — if she stumbles or is outpaced early by Barry The Worm or Master Dandy forcing their way forward, the uncontested lead scenario collapses and the entire pace map shifts.

Barry The Worm is a genuine front-end horse mapped to midfield purely by redistribution — watch how jockey Lewis Edmunds rides the first furlong; if he pushes up, a pace duel with White Umbrella becomes live and speeds up the race dramatically.

Sunlit Sea (Sir Mark Prescott, fresh off 13-day turnaround, in form) is the most dangerous horse operating from a prominent position — if she travels sweetly in second or third, her finishing record on similar going makes her the biggest danger to the leader late.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Master Dandy, Thanks Dad, Alafdhal, Trust Sergei, On Key, Porfin, Last Outlaw) all racing out of their natural role means the midfield could be extremely congested — jockeys on horses drawn wide may benefit from a clearer run through the final two furlongs.

Teardrops with the 7lb claimer Myla Coppins is worth tracking for market moves — Tony Carroll is 10/39 in his last 14 days and the horse's Standard-going form (3 wins, 8 places) is the strongest place record in the field.

races.name: Dapper Gee Gee Owners Handicap

runners_data.name: Blue Lancero
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type returning from a lengthy 272-day absence, which is a significant fitness question mark on an AW sprint; his sim-going record shows 1 win and 0 places from 3 runs, and at 4yo he is lightly raced with limited evidence of Wolverhampton competitiveness.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a long absence after finding the start unhelpful at Southwell last time, where he was well beaten in a novice; effective over seven furlongs and dropping to today's shorter trip could suit; open to improvement and acts on sound going. The layoff is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Shalaa Asker
runners_data.note: Excellent recent form at course and distance (1/5f/STA 24 days ago) and a 4W/11P record in similar going makes her the dominant pace influence; the tongue-strap is noted and she travels prominently — as the sole front-runner here she gets an uncontested lead, which suits her record ideally.
runners_data.comment: Back to his best at Lingfield last time, landing a handicap by a neck off a 2lb lower mark, and the 2lb rise looks well within range for him here; effective at five to seven furlongs on any surface and fitted with first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces. One of the main dangers.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane rides a horse with consistent placed form (2-3-3-2 recent) at 5f on various going types, and the cheekpieces may sharpen his response; he is a true hold-up type who will need to reel in Shalaa Asker from behind, and his 1W/3P in sim-going gives him the strongest closing credentials of the chasers.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated here, drawing clear with the runner-up at Ffos Las last time before going down by a length and a half off his current mark; suited to five furlongs on any surface with a top course jockey aboard and first-time blinkers potentially sharpening the effort. The one to beat.

runners_data.name: Style King
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes over on a horse whose natural hold-up style has been pushed to the map's midfield tier because the rear is crowded; his best recent effort was 2/6f/STA and he steps back to 5f where his sim-going record is modest (1W/4P from 15), and the out-of-role placement reduces confidence in his chance here.
runners_data.comment: A step up at Lingfield last time when the headgear sparked him, beaten 2¼ lengths off a mark 3lb higher; back on a lower mark now with first-time cheekpieces applied and fast AW going that suits. Inconsistent of late but holds a live chance here.

runners_data.name: The Fixer
runners_data.note: Carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag and has posted a string of poor recent efforts (0-0-0-10-11) with a 91-day break adding further concern; though his true style is hold-up, his place on the map reflects redistribution rather than natural position, and the finish-fade tag makes him hard to recommend in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive unplaced efforts are a concern, the latest at Doncaster where being drawn on the wrong side cost him; effective at five to six furlongs on AW but a trainer currently without a strike and a brief break to freshen up make this a hard proposition. A significant upturn in form is required.

races.paceDynamic: Shalaa Asker is the lone confirmed front-runner in this five-runner 5f sprint on Wolverhampton's standard AW surface, and with no genuine challenger likely to contest the lead, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without pressure. The remaining four runners — Blue Lancero, Level Up, Style King, and The Fixer — are all hold-up types by profile, meaning Shalaa Asker effectively sets the terms unchallenged while the field organises itself behind her. With no pace battle to burn her off the front, Shalaa Asker's strong course and distance form (4W11P in sim-going, recent 1/5f/STA) makes her a powerful force in this shape, and the absence of a pace rival is a significant tactical advantage. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a powerful late run and enough class to reel in a wire-to-wire leader who has been allowed to bowl along at her own tempo — but critically, the three redistibuted hold-up horses (Style King, The Fixer, Level Up) that might theoretically pounce must generate that finish from behind a horse who has not been pressured, and that is a harder task than it looks in a truly short 5f.

scenarios.title: Shalaa Asker Leads Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Shalaa Asker breaks cleanly and controls a steady, uncontested pace from the front throughout.
scenarios.body: If Shalaa Asker breaks cleanly and controls a steady, uncontested pace from the front throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to leave Shalaa Asker vulnerable in the final 100 yards and a hold-up horse produces a genuine late thrust.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fast enough to leave Shalaa Asker vulnerable in the final 100 yards and a hold-up horse produces a genuine late thrust.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos Midfield Stir
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up types (Style King, The Fixer) push forward to claim midfield ground and create a more contested early pace than expected.
scenarios.body: If the redistributed hold-up types (Style King, The Fixer) push forward to claim midfield ground and create a more contested early pace than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Flounders, Front Survives Easier
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses are collectively outpaced on standard ground and the late run never fully materialises.
scenarios.body: If the hold-up horses are collectively outpaced on standard ground and the late run never fully materialises.

watchPoints.text: Shalaa Asker's clean break is critical — if she misses the kick and is headed by an unexpected front-runner from the field, her entire race shape advantage evaporates.
Blue Lancero's 272-day absence means fitness is genuinely uncertain; watch the market and paddock for signs he is not forward enough to produce his best at the end of five furlongs.

Style King and The Fixer are both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if they push forward on-course to claim positions, they could create an uncharacteristically muddled early race shape that disrupts Level Up's run through.

Level Up has been placed in five of his last seven starts and carries Billy Loughnane, one of the more active short-priced jockeys on the circuit — watch for him to close strongly if Shalaa Asker sets a retrievable tempo.

The Fixer's fades-in-finish flag combined with a 91-day layoff makes him a major spectator candidate — monitor whether he shows any early signs of life, as an unusually forward move from him would be a significant race-shape red flag.

races.name: Thanks To TC Titch & The Team From SFRacing Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Skellig Isle
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a recent win over 5f at Wolverhampton on Standard — the step back up to 7f is a query, but Cieren Fallon's booking adds confidence and similar-going form reads adequately; will need the pace to be honest enough to make ground from rear.
runners_data.comment: Showing her best form at shorter trips, Skellig Isle found the going softer than ideal at Yarmouth last time and tired in the closing stages; she can be inconsistent but has the ability to be involved when conditions suit, and the inside draw is useful.

runners_data.name: Harbour Vision
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran who knows this track well (15/15 similar-going runs) but whose form string shows persistent fading finishes in the closing stages — the ⚠ fade flag is a serious concern at 7f and Kieran O'Neill must get him covered up early.
runners_data.comment: Back to some form last time here over course and distance, Harbour Vision tops our figures and first-time blinkers could help him build on that performance; he is a tricky customer, though, and a cold trainer run of form introduces some doubt.

runners_data.name: Cooramook
runners_data.note: Arrives on a 51-day break wearing a hood, and while trainer Mark Loughnane is cold at 0/17 in the 14-day window, the horse has placed four times in similar going at this track; however, its natural rear-running style has been pushed closer to midfield by the congested hold-up group, meaning it will not be racing as it prefers.
runners_data.comment: Despite suffering early interference last time here, Cooramook came down beaten only 3 lengths off a mark 1lb above today’s — arguably a better effort than the bare result suggests; first-time blinkers and a top course jockey boost her claims after a short break.

runners_data.name: Bomb Squad
runners_data.note: The clear pace-setter — three wins and 11 placings from 15 similar-going runs underlines his love of this surface, and a recent win over 7f at Wolverhampton confirms the trip; Finley Marsh should have him settled immediately and allowed to roll along at his own tempo.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race at Southwell off a lower mark earlier in the campaign and ran his race again last time, going down by 3 lengths from the same mark; first-time cheekpieces and a trainer in form strengthen Bomb Squad’s case as a clear danger.

runners_data.name: Pearly Squirrel
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has placed three times in the last five at similar going and showed well over 7f here before; William Pyle will need to navigate the traffic created by several other closers forced into this race shape, but the horse's consistent placing record gives it a live chance if the run materialises.
runners_data.comment: Hampered by interference last time here, Pearly Squirrel found the pace flagging late on and was beaten 3¼ lengths off 1lb above today’s mark; the trip back down is welcomed and she handles any surface, so that excused effort is worth bearing in mind.

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Has won twice and placed eight times in 13 similar-going starts, giving him the strongest course-form credentials alongside Bomb Squad; Jack Callan picks up the 3lb claim and the trainer's hot T14 strike rate of 5/21 is the best in the field — prominent racing style means he will be ideally positioned throughout.
runners_data.comment: Went close last time, beaten just half a length on a mark 1lb below today’s; previously landed a race at this track off a lower mark and he handles the surface well, but Split Elevens sits low on our figures despite the respectable recent run.

runners_data.name: Faster Bee
runners_data.note: Comes off a 51-day break wearing a hood and trainer Fergal O'Brien is modest at 1/8 over the 14-day window; a true hold-up horse by nature, this one is positioned closer than ideal due to the overcrowded rear, which reduces the effectiveness of its usual late swooping style.
runners_data.comment: Landed a race here off a lower mark earlier in the season, but Faster Bee ran very free last time and was beaten 14 lengths; he handles this surface and trip and wears first-time tongue-tie after a short break, though the revised mark needs more.

runners_data.name: Clover Time
runners_data.note: Has never won in five starts at similar going (0W5P), and the lack of a course win tempers expectations despite the place record; this horse races with a hood and is a genuine hold-up type that has been mapped closer than natural — a further complication on top of an already moderate winning profile.
runners_data.comment: Went off too freely when stepped up in trip here last time and failed to stay, beaten 10 lengths; Clover Time arrives with a cold trainer run and is ranked last on our figures, though first-time cheekpieces and an easing mark are minor positives after a short break.

runners_data.name: Lessay
runners_data.note: Ashley Lewis takes the 5lb claim and the horse has a decent 1W4P record in 15 similar-going starts, but Patrick Morris has a cool 0/3 in the T14 window and the horse's tendency to race at the rear is compromised by the field's hold-up congestion — needs things to go right.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form here last time from a mark 1lb above today’s, going down by 2 lengths; Lessay has been in better form in recent outings and handles the surface well over this trip, with first-time cheekpieces a potential aid.

runners_data.name: Mythical Isle
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard at Wolverhampton recently, which is the obvious positive, and Paddy Bradley rides; however, OR 53 is the lowest in the field, and as a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield position in a race dominated by closer types, the style-fit discount and weak trainer T14 (0/3) significantly limit confidence.
runners_data.comment: Won over course and distance last time by three-quarters of a length, digging deep to last home; Mythical Isle can blow hot and cold but is still lightly campaigned at 7f on the all-weather and must back up that display in handicap company.

races.paceDynamic: Bomb Squad is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on Standard Wolverhampton turf. Split Elevens is the only other horse with a prominent profile, likely to sit just off Bomb Squad's shoulder and provide some company without seriously pressing the pace. The result is a race run at a measured, even tempo — not a true test of stamina, not a sprint finish, but a steady-to-fair gallop that should reward horses who can travel in behind and produce a clean sustained run from two furlongs out. This shape firmly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can find a position without losing too much ground, as the lack of genuine pace pressure means the leader will coast and finish strong. The field holds substantially more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Cooramook, Faster Bee, Clover Time, Lessay, and Mythical Isle are all true hold-up types who will be forced wide or closer to the pace than ideal, with Bomb Squad and Split Elevens the most likely to actually secure their natural positions.

scenarios.title: Bomb Squad Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bomb Squad leads unopposed at a comfortable tempo and is never seriously pressured through the first five furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Bomb Squad leads unopposed at a comfortable tempo and is never seriously pressured through the first five furlongs.

scenarios.body: If Split Elevens is ridden more aggressively and actively challenges Bomb Squad from the three-furlong pole, injecting a meaningful duel.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and one of the repositioned closers finds a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and one of the repositioned closers finds a clear run in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is faster than anticipated, burning off the front pair, and a low-rated closer benefits from the carnage.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is faster than anticipated, burning off the front pair, and a low-rated closer benefits from the carnage.

watchPoints.text: Bomb Squad is the sole front-runner and Finley Marsh must not allow him to be bullied off the lead by Split Elevens in the early stages — if he gets to stride freely, his record makes him very hard to beat.

Split Elevens represents the biggest danger to Bomb Squad — watch whether Jack Callan sends him forward aggressively to test the pace-setter, as a contested lead would meaningfully change the race shape.

Five genuine hold-up horses (Cooramook, Faster Bee, Clover Time, Lessay, Mythical Isle) are all out of their natural positions — monitor the draw and early movement to identify which, if any, can actually find clear daylight in the straight.

Harbour Vision's fade-in-finish flag is particularly relevant over 7f on an all-weather surface that rewards sustained galloping — backers should watch for any signs of dropping away inside the final two furlongs.

Skellig Isle's last two wins have come at 5f, so watch closely whether Cieren Fallon settles the horse in a position to build into the longer 7f trip, as it may be vulnerable if it races too freely early.
